subject: physics

hotspots.label: Block
hotspots.description: The object whose height stores gravitational potential energy.
hotspots.colorHint: Warm wooden block resting on the shelf.
hotspots.function: Holds stored energy decided by its height and mass.

hotspots.label: Shelf
hotspots.description: The support whose height you lift — raising it stores more energy in the block.
hotspots.colorHint: A light tower shelf arm at the left.
hotspots.function: Sets the height input of potential energy.

hotspots.label: Stored-Energy Meter
hotspots.description: The joule readout that climbs as the shelf lifts — PE = mgh in numbers.
hotspots.colorHint: A vertical gauge beside the shelf.

hotspots.label: Height Guide
hotspots.description: The vertical scale measuring the block's height above the floor.
hotspots.colorHint: A slim ruler behind the tower.
hotspots.function: Shows the height term feeding the formula.

hotspots.label: Release Button
hotspots.description: Tap to drop the block and watch stored potential energy cash out into falling motion.
hotspots.colorHint: Ring-like amber button in the floor corner.
hotspots.function: Starts the fall and the energy conversion.

visualStyleNotes: Warm off-white paper background, soft vignette. A pastel floor and a two-post shelf tower, a warm wooden block, a green stored-energy meter, and a height guide. Saturated color only on the block and meter needle.
materialNotes: Roughness ~0.55 warm wood for block and posts; meter face pale with a green needle. No emissive, no bloom.
assetBrief:
SUBJECT: gravitational potential energy banking on height.

GEOMETRY: a floor plane; a two-post shelf tower (posts x=-0.6/+0.6) with a height guide behind; a wooden block (0,1.4,0) resting on the shelf; a green meter (1.2,1.5,0) and a round release button (-0.3,0.4,1.4).

INTERACTION: drag the shelf up/down (height) → meter = m×g×h; release lowers the shelf, animating the block's fall as meter drains.

NAMED NODES: Floor, PostL, PostR, Shelf, Block, HeightGuide, PE_Meter, ReleaseButton. 7-9k tris.
